note_to_agent: The Application's own spec.syncPolicy.syncOptions genuinely includes 'CreateNamespace=true'. Diagnose why the sync failed anyway, and what you'd do next.

reference_answer.root_cause: Triggering a sync via a raw `kubectl patch application --type merge -p '{"operation":{"sync":{}}}'` does not populate the operation's own syncOptions from the Application's spec -- the operation object created was a bare empty sync ({}), which does not carry CreateNamespace=true forward from spec.syncPolicy.syncOptions the way a normal `argocd app sync` CLI/UI-triggered sync would. ArgoCD's own reconciler only creates the namespace as part of a sync operation that actually carries that option.
reference_answer.fix_applied: Manually ran `kubectl create namespace mimir`, then re-triggered the same sync patch. All resources applied successfully on the retry since the namespace now existed independent of the sync operation's own options.
reference_answer.verification: kubectl get pods -n mimir showed a real pod scheduled and starting after the fix.
